repo_model.summary: This is a RelBench generic-search starter workspace. The root candidate loads a task from the sanitized cache and writes baseline NumPy predictions, while the provided helpers and immutable grader enforce prediction contracts, official validation scoring, and rolling/full-run evaluation.

entrypoints.how_to_run: python main.py --debug for the fast/debug run, or python main.py for the full run
With the evaluator environment configured: python kapso_evaluation/grader.py --fidelity fast|full [--fraction F] [--seed S]

where_to_edit.role: Primary solution file: replace the trivial task-family branches with data loading, feature construction, training, and prediction logic.
Reusable task-loading, output-saving, temporal-safety, and recommendation-metric helpers.
Evaluation contract to consult before changing prediction shapes, files, or data access.

claims.statement: The current root candidate is an intentionally trivial RelBench baseline: it reads dataset and task identity from the environment, loads the task with downloads disabled, and is intended to be replaced by a real solution.

evidence.description: Identifies the file as a baseline candidate.
Instructs the user to replace the baseline with a real solution.

claims.statement: kapso_datasets.common.load_task builds a TaskContext containing the dataset, task, database, and train/validation/test RelBench tables; save_predictions centralizes writing the two required NumPy artifacts.

evidence.description: Obtains the database with the configured timestamp cutoff.
Loads train, validation, and test tables.

claims.statement: Prediction generation branches by task family: recommendation returns tiled integer ranks, binary classification returns 0.5, multiclass classification returns uniform class scores, and other tasks return the training-target median.

evidence.description: Handles remaining task types as regression-like tasks.

claims.statement: The candidate writes predictions under KAPSO_RUN_DATA_DIR; ordinary runs write both validation and test arrays, while rolling ticks intentionally write only test predictions for later evaluator assembly.

evidence.description: Saves the assembled full prediction vector.

claims.statement: The immutable grader runs main.py in an isolated subprocess, validates the produced arrays, computes official validation metrics, and archives full-fidelity predictions and candidate code.

evidence.description: States that the grader runs main.py as an isolated child.
Describes validation scoring and run archiving.

claims.statement: The harness expects val_predictions.npy and test_predictions.npy after every ordinary candidate run, including debug, with rows positionally aligned to the corresponding RelBench tables; validation predictions must be out-of-sample.

evidence.description: Requires both prediction files after every run.
Requires validation predictions to be out-of-sample.
Restricts train-plus-validation fitting to the test-producing model.

claims.statement: Required prediction formats are binary float probabilities of shape (N,) in [0,1], regression floats of shape (N,), multiclass floats of shape (N,C), and recommendation integer rankings of shape (N,K) containing distinct destination IDs in range.

evidence.description: Defines binary, regression, and multiclass formats.
Checks recommendation shape and integer dtype.

claims.statement: The search score is the official primary metric on the complete validation split; test labels and test metrics are unavailable inside this evaluation loop.

evidence.description: Defines the search score as the official validation primary metric.
States that test metrics are private.
States that test labels are physically absent.
Computes metrics from validation predictions and the validation table.
Places the selected primary validation metric in the manifest score.

claims.statement: RelBench data must be loaded with download=False from the sanitized, read-only cache; candidate code must not attempt to fetch data or probe for test labels.

evidence.description: Requires the RelBench API with download=False.
Describes the sanitized read-only cache and absent test labels.
Documents loading from the sanitized cache without downloads.

claims.statement: In rolling evaluation, each snapshot is evaluated independently, each tick's test prediction length must match its indices, and the grader scatters the tick outputs back into the official row order.

evidence.description: Documents one candidate invocation per rolling tick.
Copies each rolling snapshot into an isolated cache.
Checks tick prediction length against tick indices.
Scatters concatenated predictions using flat indices.

claims.statement: The basic end-to-end check is to run python main.py --debug from the repository root, followed by python main.py for the full training run; both runs are scored after prediction files are written.

evidence.description: States that the harness runs from the repository root.
Builds the debug or full candidate command.

claims.statement: After writing predictions, run python kapso_datasets/check_predictions.py to catch missing files, shape and dtype mismatches, non-finite values, and binary range violations before official scoring.

evidence.description: Checks both validation and test splits.

claims.statement: Fast and full evaluator modes score the complete official validation split rather than a fraction of rows; the official metrics and machine-readable manifest are printed on success.

evidence.description: Maps fast fidelity to the debug candidate run.
Maps full fidelity to the full candidate run.
States that the scored item set never shrinks.

claims.statement: In the current baseline, --debug does not change data processing or prediction construction; it is only reflected in the final debug status print.

evidence.description: Prediction logic begins without checking debug mode.
The final status message is where debug is inspected.

claims.statement: The baseline treats a missing or empty validation parquet in the cache as rolling mode, sets validation row count to zero, and skips writing validation predictions; this behavior only works because the rolling grader assembles final arrays from tick outputs.

evidence.description: Documents empty validation tables in rolling snapshots.
Uses zero validation rows when the file is absent.
Derives rolling mode from zero validation rows.
Skips validation output in rolling mode.
Reads only tick test predictions during rolling execution.
Writes assembled outputs after collecting all ticks.

claims.statement: Recommendation baseline rows are always the IDs 0 through eval_k-1 and are not checked against task.num_dst_nodes; the checker warns about out-of-range or duplicate IDs rather than failing them.

evidence.description: Tiles those IDs for every row.
Warns rather than fails for out-of-range IDs.
Warns rather than fails for duplicate IDs.

claims.statement: The candidate and evaluator require NumPy and RelBench; the provided evaluation suite is otherwise self-contained in the Python standard library plus those packages.

evidence.description: States that Python with relbench and numpy is sufficient.

claims.statement: Runtime configuration is supplied through environment variables, especially RELBENCH_DATASET, RELBENCH_TASK, RELBENCH_CACHE_DIR, and KAPSO_RUN_DATA_DIR; the grader also requires the primary metric, work directory, and fidelity-specific timeouts.

book.summary: This is a RelBench generic-search starter workspace. The root candidate loads a task from the sanitized cache and writes baseline NumPy predictions, while the provided helpers and immutable grader enforce prediction contracts, official validation scoring, and rolling/full-run evaluation.

toc.title: Architecture
toc.one_liner: Root candidate, reusable RelBench helpers, and an isolated official evaluator form the end-to-end pipeline.

toc.title: Entrypoints
toc.one_liner: Run the candidate from the repository root, or invoke the provided evaluator with its fidelity mode.

toc.title: Where to edit
toc.one_liner: Implement the candidate in main.py and optionally consume the provided helper API.

toc.title: Invariants
toc.one_liner: Prediction files, alignment, task-specific shapes, and validation-only scoring are hard correctness requirements.

toc.title: Testing
toc.one_liner: Use the debug run, prediction self-checker, and official grader output to validate changes.

toc.title: Gotchas
toc.one_liner: The baseline has rolling-specific behavior and deliberately weak predictions that can violate task-level recommendation quality constraints.

toc.title: Dependencies
toc.one_liner: The runtime depends on Python, NumPy, RelBench, and evaluator-provided environment variables.
